title: セイバールート七日目-07

pages.ja:

話していたら体の熱も下がった事だし、そろそろ打ち合いを再開するか。
pages.jaRuby:
……さて。
話していたら体の熱も下がった事だし、そろそろ打ち合いを再開するか。
pages.en:
…Well, then.

Talking has given my body time to cool down. We should probably resume our match.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Well.
Talking has cooled me down, so let’s continue with the training.
I’m skipping school, so I should acquaint my body with fighting as much as time allows.

pages.ja:
「セイバー、始めよう。休憩はもういいよ」
「……そうなのですか？ 見たところ体の熱は下がったようですが、痛みの方はまだ治まっていないでしょう？」
pages.jaRuby:
「セイバー、始めよう。休憩はもういいよ」
「……そうなのですか？ 見たところ体の熱は下がったようですが、痛みの方はまだ治まっていないでしょう？」
pages.en:
“Saber, let's start again. I've rested long enough.”

“…Are you certain? Your body no longer appears overheated, but the pain cannot have subsided yet.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Saber, let’s start. I’ve rested enough.”
“…Is that so? It looks as if you have cooled down, but your pain has not yet gone away, right?”

pages.ja:
「構わないよ、そんなの。ただの打ち身なんだから、多少の痛みは我慢する。今の俺はほっとけば治るんだから」
「しかし、それで悪化しては鍛錬の意味がない。もうしばらくは様子を見るべきだと思いますが」
pages.jaRuby:
「構わないよ、そんなの。ただの打ち身なんだから、多少の痛みは我慢する。今の俺はほっとけば治るんだから」
「しかし、それで悪化しては鍛錬の意味がない。もうしばらくは様子を見るべきだと思いますが」
pages.en:
“That doesn't matter. They're only bruises. I can put up with a little pain, and the way I am now, they'll heal if I leave them alone.”

“But if you aggravate your injuries, the training will have been for nothing. I believe we should wait a little longer.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I don’t care. They’re just bruises, so I’ll bear a little pain. I can heal automatically now.”
“But there is no point in training if it worsens. I believe we should wait a bit longer and see.”

pages.ja: 「いいからいいから。遠坂が帰ってくるまでにやっときたいんだ。アイツにはこんな姿見せられないだろ」
pages.jaRuby: 「いいからいいから。遠坂が帰ってくるまでにやっときたいんだ。アイツにはこんな姿見せられないだろ」
pages.en: “It's fine, really. I want to get this done before Tohsaka comes home. I can't let her see me in this condition, can I?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Don’t worry. I want to finish this before Tohsaka gets home. We can’t have her see me like this, right?”

pages.ja:
「……ふう。分かりました、確かにいずれ敵となる凛に、シロウの腕前を知られるのはよくありませんね。
多少無茶とは思いますが、そういう事でしたらペースをあげていきましょう」
pages.jaRuby:
「……ふう。分かりました、確かにいずれ敵となる凛に、シロウの腕前を知られるのはよくありませんね。
多少無茶とは思いますが、そういう事でしたらペースをあげていきましょう」
pages.en:
“…Very well. It would indeed be unwise to reveal your present ability to Rin, who will eventually become our enemy.

“I believe you are pushing yourself too far, but under the circumstances, we shall increase the pace.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Sigh. I understand. It is certainly not good to have Rin, our eventual enemy, find out your powers.
I believe it is a bit excessive, but if that is the case, let us bring the pace up a little.”

pages.ja:
ひょい、と落ちていた竹刀を拾うセイバー。
と。
間の抜けた音が道場に響き渡った。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Saber stoops and lightly retrieves the bamboo sword from the floor.

Then a remarkably foolish sound echoes through the dojo.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Saber picks up the shinai.
And then.
A strange sound echoes through the dojo.

pages.ja:
「セイバー……？」
その、今のはセイバーの、腹の音だと思うのだが。
「空腹のようです。鍛錬に夢中で気が付きませんでした」
pages.jaRuby:
「セイバー……？」
その、今のはセイバーの、腹の音だと思うのだが。
「空腹のようです。鍛錬に夢中で気が付きませんでした」
pages.en:
“Saber…?”

I am fairly certain that came from her stomach.

“It appears I am hungry. I was too absorbed in our training to notice.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Saber…?”
Um, I think that was Saber’s stomach.
“I believe I am hungry. I did not notice since I was so engrossed in training.”

pages.ja:
「あ
うん。そう言えばもう昼か」
そりゃお腹の虫ぐらい鳴るよな。
俺はまだそうでもないけど、セイバーがそんなに空腹なら昼飯にしておこう。
その間にこっちの体も完治してくれれば御の字だし。

pages.en:
“Ah——right. Come to think of it, it's already noon.”

No wonder her stomach is growling.

I am not especially hungry yet, but if Saber is, we should stop for lunch. With any luck, my body will finish healing in the meantime.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Ohyeah. Now that you mention it, it’s lunchtime already.”
No wonder her stomach has started growling.
I’m not that hungry yet, but if Saber’s hungry, let’s have lunch.
It’ll be good if my body heals in that time as well.

pages.ja:
「いいや、ちょうどいいし昼にしよう。ささっと材料買ってくるから、セイバーは居間で休んでいてくれ」
「シロウ。外出するなら私も付き添いますが」
pages.jaRuby:
「いいや、ちょうどいいし昼にしよう。ささっと材料買ってくるから、セイバーは居間で休んでいてくれ」
「シロウ。外出するなら私も付き添いますが」
pages.en:
“No, this is perfect. Let's have lunch. I'll run out and buy the ingredients, so you can rest in the living room.”

“Shirou. If you intend to leave the house, I will accompany you.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“All right. It’s a good time, so let’s have lunch. I’ll go buy some groceries, so you can rest in the living room.”
“Shirou, I shall escort you if you are going outside.”

pages.ja:
「大丈夫、すぐ近くの商店街だ。真っ昼間から襲いかかってくるヤツはいないし、セイバーがいたら逆に目立つよ」
「…………本当に、危険はないのですね？」
「ないって。すぐに帰ってくるから待っててくれ」

pages.en:
“I'll be fine. The shopping district is just down the road. No one is going to attack me in broad daylight, and having you there would only draw attention.”

“…There is truly no danger?”

“None. I'll be right back, so wait here.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s fine, I’m only going to the shopping district nearby. There’s no one who would attack me in the daytime, and we’d rather stand out if you were with me.”
“…There is really no danger?”
“No. I’ll come back right away, so please wait here.”

pages.ja:
財布を持って外に出る。
ここから商店街まで、自転車でざっと十分もかからない。
ちなみにいま車庫から持ち出したのは二号機で、一号機は柳洞寺前に路駐したままである。

pages.en:
I take my wallet and leave the house.

The shopping district is less than ten minutes away by bicycle.

For the record, this is bicycle number two. Number one remains illegally parked in front of Ryuudou Temple.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I take my wallet and go outside.
It won’t take even ten minutes on a bicycle to get to the shopping district from here.
By the way, the bicycle I just took from the garage is bicycle number two. Number one is still out in front of the Ryuudou Temple.

pages.ja:
坂道を下っていく。
平日の昼間に商店街に行くなんて、子供の頃のお使い以来かもしれない。
pages.jaRuby:
坂道を下っていく。
平日の昼間に商店街に行くなんて、子供の頃のお使い以来かもしれない。
pages.en:
I coast down the hill.

I may not have visited the shopping district in the middle of a weekday since I was a child running errands.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I descend the hill.
I don’t think I’ve been to the shopping district in the daytime on a weekday since I was running errands as a child.

pages.ja:
さすがに昼間という事もあり、交差点には買い物帰りの主婦さんが多い。
奥さんたちが歩いてくる深山町の中心が、俺や桜が愛用しているご近所の商店街である。

pages.en:
As one would expect at this hour, the intersection is crowded with housewives on their way home from shopping.

The heart of Miyama, toward which they are all walking, is the neighborhood shopping district Sakura and I frequent.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Because it’s daytime, there are lots of housewives at the intersection, on their way home from shopping.
They’re coming from the shopping district that Sakura and I go to regularly.

pages.ja:
とりあえず、一通り買い物を済ませてきた。
二人分の昼食の材料と、軽い和菓子。
今日の夕食は遠坂の担当だからいいにしても、明日の朝用の食パンを四人分。
イチゴのジャムの作り方なんて知らないので、一番安い……のは何かと物議を醸しそうだから、それなりに値の張った物を買った。

pages.en:
For now, I finish all the necessary shopping.

I buy ingredients for lunch for two, along with a few Japanese sweets. Tohsaka is responsible for dinner, so that can wait, but I also need enough bread for four people tomorrow morning.

I have no idea how to make strawberry jam. I consider buying the cheapest jar, decide that would probably start an argument, and settle for something respectably expensive.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I finish buying all the groceries.
Ingredients for lunch for two, and a light Japanese snack.
Dinner tonight is fine since Tohsaka’s in charge of that, but I buy enough bread for four people for tomorrow’s breakfast.
I don’t know how to make strawberry jam, so I buy the cheapest… no that’ll probably get me some criticism, so I buy a rather expensive one.

pages.ja:
「……くそ、ひどい出費だ。なんだってこんな甘ったるいモンの為に千円も払わなくちゃいけないんだ」
文句を言いつつ自転車の籠に荷物を押し込む。
と。
くいくい、と後ろから服を引っ張られる感じがした。

pages.en:
“…Damn, that hurt. Why do I have to spend a thousand yen on something this sickeningly sweet?”

Still complaining, I stuff the groceries into my bicycle basket.

——Then I feel someone tugging at my clothes from behind.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Damn, it’s really expensive. Why do I have to pay a thousand yen for something so sweet?”
I complain as I put the groceries into the bicycle cart.
And then.
I feel something tugging at my clothes from behind.

pages.ja:
「？」
なんだろ、と振り返る。
そこには。
銀の髪をした、幼い少女の姿があった。
pages.jaRuby:
「？」
なんだろ、と振り返る。
そこには。
銀の髪をした、幼い少女の姿があった。
pages.en:
“?”

I turn to see what it is.

Standing there is a little girl with silver hair.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…?”
I turn around, wondering what it could be.
There.
Is a young girl with silver hair.

pages.ja:

！」
がらがっしょん、と自転車を倒しながら後じさる。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Y-You——!”

I stumble backward, knocking the bicycle over with a tremendous crash.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What, you’re!?”
I back off, knocking the bicycle over.

pages.en:
I fall instinctively into a fighting stance.

The girl merely smiles at me.
pages.mirrorMoon: I stand ready at once while the girl just smiles at me.

pages.ja:
「……？」
少女からは殺気というか、敵意がまったく感じられない。
あまつさえ少女は、
「よかった。生きてたんだね、お兄ちゃん」
なんて、嬉しげな笑みをうかべてきやがった。

pages.en:
“…?”

I sense no killing intent from her—no hostility of any kind.

Worse still, she gives me a delighted smile.

“I'm so glad. You're alive, Big Brother.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…?”
I don’t feel any murderous intent nor even enmity from that girl.
In addition, the girl says,
“I’m glad. You’re alive, Onii-chan.”
And she smiles happily.

あの夜、俺を一刀のもとに斬り伏せた怪物の主。
それと、事もあろうにご近所の商店街で、しかも真昼間から遭遇するなんて誰が思おう。

pages.en:
“——”

…This girl is unquestionably Berserker's Master.

She commands the monster who struck me down in a single blow that night.

Who could have imagined I would encounter her in my own neighborhood shopping district, in the middle of the day?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“!”
…This girl is definitely Berserker’s Master.
The master of the monster that slashed me in one blow that night.
Who would expect to meet someone like this in a shopping district near their house, especially in daytime?

pages.ja:
「まさか
ここで、やる気か」
「？ おかしなコトを言うんだね。お日さまが出ているうちに戦っちゃダメなんだから」
むー、と不満そうに口をとがらす。
それは、どう見ても年相応の、幼い少女の仕草だった。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“You can't mean——are you planning to fight me here?”

“? What a strange thing to say. We're not allowed to fight while the sun is out.”

She pouts in dissatisfaction.

No matter how I look at it, it is the gesture of an ordinary girl her age.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Don’t tell me… you intend to fight me here?”
“…? You’re saying strange things. We can’t fight while the sun’s up.”
She frowns in displeasure.
That is definitely the behavior of a young girl, suitable for her age.

」

“——”

I have no idea what she intends.

But even I can tell that, whatever her intentions may be, the girl before me is harmless at this moment.

たしか、えっと」
「イリヤスフィール・フォン・アインツベルン。長いからイリヤでいいよ。それで、お兄ちゃんはなんて名前？」

pages.en:
“Y-You're… what was it again?”

“Illyasviel von Einzbern. It's long, so you can call me Illya. What's your name, Big Brother?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Y-You’reif I remember correctly, uh…”
“Illyasviel von Einzbern. It’s long, so you can call me Illya. So what’s Onii-chan’s name?”

pages.ja:
「俺……？ 俺は衛宮士郎だけど」
「エミヤシロ？ なんか言いにくい名前だね、それ」
pages.jaRuby:

“Me…? I'm Shirou Emiya.”

“Emiya Shiro? That's rather hard to say.”

“Me…? I’m Emiya Shirou.”
“Emiyashiro? That’s hard to say.”

pages.jaRuby: 「……俺もそんな発音で言われたのは初めてだ。いいよ、覚えにくかったら士郎でいい。そっちが名前だ」

pages.mirrorMoon: “…It’s the first time I’ve heard it pronounced like that too. No, if you have trouble remembering it, you can call me Shirou. That’s my name.”

Illyasviel gives me a strangely suggestive look.

“Shirou? Oh, so it’s an easier name than I thought. I see, Shirou. …Yeah, that sounds good. It’s simple, but it sounds aloof.”
Illyasviel looks at me with suggestive eyes.

その気になれば、お隣の花屋さんもろとも俺を吹っ飛ばせるだろう。

pages.en:
“——…!”

My body reacts before my mind does. I lower my center of gravity, ready to move at any instant.

…She is Berserker's Master, after all. If she wished, she could probably blow me away together with the flower shop next door.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…!”
My body unintentionally moves and lowers its waist down so it can move more freely.
…Because she is Berserker’s Master.
If she felt like it, she probably could blow me away along with the flower shop next to me.
